hypotheses.justification: If ι is empty, EuclideanSpace ℝ ι is a subsingleton: two points agree at every coordinate because there are none. So any K has at most one element, and the conclusion holds trivially. Proof without the binder: split on `isEmpty_or_nonempty ι`. In the empty case take α = 1 (this gives 0 < α and α ≤ 1). For any Omega, a, u, K take C = 0 and close the goal with `Set.Subsingleton.holderOnWith` (Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Holder.lean: `(hs : s.Subsingleton) (C r) (f) : HolderOnWith C r f s`), with `hs` given by `Set.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`; none of the other hypotheses are used. In the nonempty case the existing proof via `exists_holderOnWith_preciseRepresentative_of_isCompact_drift` works unchanged. [Nonempty ι] is mentioned nowhere else in the statement, so it can be deleted.
